answer: Stake-bonded identity works like this: each agent must lock a deposit in escrow before it can bid for tasks. The deposit is tied to one vertex in the reputation graph, and an anchor contract records the lock on a public ledger. If peers prove the agent cheated, the escrow is slashed. Splitting into a thousand fakes therefore needs a thousand deposits, so an attacker pays roughly the stake, say fifty dollars of copper-priced compute credits, per identity, and loses it on detection.
